definitionYaml:
version: "1.0"
name: "evidence_bound_review"
description: "Profile C: primary + skeptic on ephemeral worker + contract gate"
inputs:
  optional:
    - evidence_pack
outputs:
  decision:
    type: object
states:
  - id: PROPOSE
    initial: true
  - id: REVIEW
  - id: FINALIZE
  - id: CLOSED
    terminal: true
transitions:
  - from: PROPOSE
    to: REVIEW
    trigger: propose_done
    guards:
      - g_propose
  - from: REVIEW
    to: FINALIZE
    trigger: review_done
    guards:
      - g_review
  - from: FINALIZE
    to: CLOSED
    trigger: finalize_done
    guards:
      - g_finalize
steps:
  - id: propose
    state: PROPOSE
    handler: primary_c
    config:
      agent_kind: vllm
      provider.model: "qwen3-coder-30b"
      provider.max_tokens: 1536
      provider.timeout_secs: 300
      see_prior: false
      num_agents: 1
      output_contract:
        contract_id: evidence-bound-decision
        format: json_object
        required_fields: [claims, decision]
        allowed_values:
          decision: [accept, reject, request_changes, request_more_evidence]
        evidence:
          claims_field: claims
          refs_field: evidence_refs
          allowed_refs_from_context: evidence_pack
      prompt: "You are the primary engineer reviewing a technical decision for the Underpass Choreographer platform. QUESTION: Should reviewer objections block final acceptance, or only lower confidence? Decide: accept (objections block until resolved), reject (objections only annotate/lower confidence), request_changes or request_more_evidence.\nEVIDENCE PACK (the ONLY citable evidence; cite by id in evidence_refs):\n- [ev-t5-skeptic-ignored] Run csi-typha-1 (real): the skeptic produced the alternative closest to the verified root cause and named the single discriminating piece of evidence to check — and the judge's verdict did not incorporate it. Non-blocking objections were ignored at synthesis time.\n- [ev-t5-rounds-not-convergence] Run csi-typha-appeal-1 (real, trace a5ed9c25…): three rounds of mandatory peer critique did not converge on evidence; critique acted as 'elaborate further'. Forcing engagement with objections does not by itself improve grounding.\n- [ev-t5-blocking-mechanism-exists] Blocking is implementable today: a failing OutputContract kills the step (NoValidProposal), the FSM guard blocks the transition, and retry_policy re-runs the step — i.e., 'objection blocks' can be encoded as policy, not as model behaviour.\n- [ev-t5-liveness-risk] A blocking reviewer creates a liveness risk: with max_attempts retries exhausted the ceremony halts short of a terminal state, and there is no request_more_evidence FSM state yet (future work noted in PR #118). Blocked-forever is a real failure mode to design for.\n- [ev-t5-reviewer-cost] The reviewer in this platform runs on the ephemeral G6 worker: blocking semantics extend worker lifetime (more GPU minutes) while non-blocking lets the reaper stop it sooner. Governance choice has a direct, measurable compute cost.\nEvery claim MUST cite at least one evidence id from the pack in its evidence_refs. CRITICAL OUTPUT FORMAT: your ENTIRE response must be raw JSON — the first character of your response must be { and the last must be }. NEVER wrap it in ``` fences. Shape: {\"claims\": [{\"text\": \"...\", \"evidence_refs\": [\"ev-...\"]}], \"decision\": \"accept|reject|request_changes|request_more_evidence\", \"risks\": [\"...\"], \"assumptions\": [\"...\"]}"
  - id: review
    state: REVIEW
    handler: skeptic_c
    config:
      agent_kind: vllm
      provider.model: "phi4-mini-aws"
      provider.max_tokens: 1024
      provider.timeout_secs: 300
      see_prior: true
      num_agents: 1
      prompt: "You are the skeptical reviewer, running on the ephemeral AWS GPU worker. The primary engineer's proposal is in the prior discussion. Do NOT synthesize an answer. For each claim: state OBJECTION (with which evidence id contradicts or is missing) or ACCEPT. Flag any claim whose evidence_refs do not support its text. End with: BLOCKING or NON-BLOCKING overall. Plain text, terse."
  - id: finalize
    state: FINALIZE
    handler: primary_c_final
    config:
      agent_kind: vllm
      provider.model: "qwen3-coder-30b"
      provider.max_tokens: 1536
      provider.timeout_secs: 300
      see_prior: true
      num_agents: 1
      output_contract:
        contract_id: evidence-bound-decision
        format: json_object
        required_fields: [claims, decision]
        allowed_values:
          decision: [accept, reject, request_changes, request_more_evidence]
        evidence:
          claims_field: claims
          refs_field: evidence_refs
          allowed_refs_from_context: evidence_pack
      prompt: "You are the primary engineer. Revise your proposal incorporating the reviewer's objections from the prior discussion (drop or fix unsupported claims; do not argue). QUESTION: Should reviewer objections block final acceptance, or only lower confidence? Decide: accept (objections block until resolved), reject (objections only annotate/lower confidence), request_changes or request_more_evidence.\nEVIDENCE PACK (the ONLY citable evidence; cite by id in evidence_refs):\n- [ev-t5-skeptic-ignored] Run csi-typha-1 (real): the skeptic produced the alternative closest to the verified root cause and named the single discriminating piece of evidence to check — and the judge's verdict did not incorporate it. Non-blocking objections were ignored at synthesis time.\n- [ev-t5-rounds-not-convergence] Run csi-typha-appeal-1 (real, trace a5ed9c25…): three rounds of mandatory peer critique did not converge on evidence; critique acted as 'elaborate further'. Forcing engagement with objections does not by itself improve grounding.\n- [ev-t5-blocking-mechanism-exists] Blocking is implementable today: a failing OutputContract kills the step (NoValidProposal), the FSM guard blocks the transition, and retry_policy re-runs the step — i.e., 'objection blocks' can be encoded as policy, not as model behaviour.\n- [ev-t5-liveness-risk] A blocking reviewer creates a liveness risk: with max_attempts retries exhausted the ceremony halts short of a terminal state, and there is no request_more_evidence FSM state yet (future work noted in PR #118). Blocked-forever is a real failure mode to design for.\n- [ev-t5-reviewer-cost] The reviewer in this platform runs on the ephemeral G6 worker: blocking semantics extend worker lifetime (more GPU minutes) while non-blocking lets the reaper stop it sooner. Governance choice has a direct, measurable compute cost.\nCRITICAL OUTPUT FORMAT: your ENTIRE response must be raw JSON — the first character of your response must be { and the last must be }. NEVER wrap it in ``` fences. Shape: {\"claims\": [{\"text\": \"...\", \"evidence_refs\": [\"ev-...\"]}], \"decision\": \"accept|reject|request_changes|request_more_evidence\", \"risks\": [\"...\"], \"assumptions\": [\"...\"]}"
guards:
  g_propose:
    type: automated
    check: "step_status:propose:COMPLETED"
  g_review:
    type: automated
    check: "step_status:review:COMPLETED"
  g_finalize:
    type: automated
    check: "step_status:finalize:COMPLETED"
roles:
  - id: PRIMARY_ENGINEER
    allowed_actions:
      - propose
      - propose_done
      - finalize
      - finalize_done
  - id: SKEPTICAL_REVIEWER
    allowed_actions:
      - review
      - review_done
timeouts:
  step_default: 600
retry_policies:
  default:
    max_attempts: 2
    backoff_seconds: 2
